subject: Umbra Health: log visibility requirements + BYOK feasibility
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@umbrahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: John Lee <j.lee@umbrahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0500
Subject: Audit log granularity + BYOK question for Dedicated PoC

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance team reviewed the notes and has two concrete asks before we can sign off on the Dedicated pilot: 

1) Audit log granularity: we need per-tenant (not per-cluster) event records for authentication, model invocation (including model version), configuration changes, and key-access events; retention must be configurable to 7/30/365 day windows. Can you confirm whether Redwood can emit separate tenant-level event streams or if we should expect to receive an aggregated cluster-level feed?

2) BYOK/KMS: Umbra must retain custody of the CMK for the pilot. Is there an existing Private/Dedicated flow that supports customer-managed KMS keys with rotation audit hooks? If not, can you outline feasibility and an estimated timeline/cost for a short-term carveout?

Attaching a spreadsheet with our compliance team's minimal fields they expect to see (column format expectations). We can be flexible on delivery format (S3 push, syslog, or streaming webhook) but need to validate ordering guarantees for forensics.

Attachments: umbra_audit_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Appreciate a short triage note and next steps by EOD Friday if possible; we have an internal review on Monday.

Best,
Sara
Compliance Manager
Umbra Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@umbrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit log granularity + BYOK question for Dedicated PoC

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet, this is helpful. Quick triage from our side: 

- Audit logs: Redwood Dedicated currently emits tenant-scoped events for auth and API invocation; however, configuration-change and KMS access events are routed through a separate infra workflow (we have cluster-level metadata attached today but not the explicit CMK access audit line-item Umbra requests).

- Retention: configurable at the tenant level is supported for 7/30/365 as policy presets, but longer-term custom retention will require a manual config change and approval (we can automate for pilots).

- BYOK/KMS: we have a Private deployment path that supports customer-managed keys (via customer KMS/HSM), with rotation hooks off the control plane. For Dedicated, we can prototype a limited BYOK flow (customer-owned CMKs with ephemeral key wrapping) but it will require a short engineering spike to add rotation audit events and the tenant-level CMK access entries Umbra needs.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Marissa, can you run a quick feasibility estimate (engineering story points + rough ETA) for adding explicit CMK access events to the Dedicated audit stream and supporting S3 push with ordering guarantees?
2) Ben, please confirm whether our current Dedicated infra can attach tenant-level CMK identifiers to every runtime invocation record (we might need a small schema change).
3) Naomi, I'll need a minimal delivery design from Security (log format + threat considerations) that we can share with Umbra.

Sara — I'll get answers to the three action items by EOD Monday and can convene a short call with our infra lead if helpful.

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Product, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit log granularity + BYOK question for Dedicated PoC

Adding details from infra POV after a quick sync with the runtime team: 

- CMK access events: feasible as a mid-sized change. We need to surface two event types: CMK-usage (when a tenant key is used to unwrap/wrap ephemeral keys) and CMK-admin (key-rotation, policy changes). Estimated 5 sprint-days of focused work (includes schema, runtime tagging, and delivery plumbing).

- Delivery options: S3 push with sequence numbering is the fastest to implement for a pilot; streaming webhooks require idempotency logic on Umbra's side and more infra work. We can support syslog if Umbra prefers.

- Ordering/forensics: sequence numbers + per-tenant monotonic counters will be included in the S3 batches; we can also include per-event causality ids to help with distributed tracing.

Open questions for product/security: 
- Naomi, what are the minimum fields Security wants in every CMK event? (I can map to the spreadsheet columns if you share.)
- Marcus, do we want to surface this as a short-term Dedicated carveout (pilot) or push Umbra toward Private for full BYOK support? Pilot timeline: if we start immediately, first delivery in ~3 weeks.

Attachments: none

-Marissa
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit log granularity + BYOK question for Dedicated PoC

Thanks — quick security checklist and recommended minimal CMK event fields for the pilot: 

Required fields (pilot): tenant_id, event_timestamp (ISO8601), event_type (CMK_USAGE | CMK_ADMIN), operation_id, initiator_principal (service/user), key_id (tenant-visible id), model_id, model_version, invocation_id (if applicable), retention_policy_tag, sequence_number, checksum

Optional fields: caller_ip, user_agent, trace_id, request_payload_hash (for partial-data repro)

Risk notes: ensure key_id in events is a tenant-visible opaque identifier (no plaintext CMK material). Rotation events must not leak previous key material and must include rotation_authority and rotation_method.

I'm comfortable with the 3-week pilot if infra can provide S3 batches with sequence numbers and the CMK_USAGE/CMK_ADMIN event types. Marissa — please add the engineering owner and schedule for the spike; Marcus — I'll prep a brief one-page for Umbra outlining the security assumptions and what we can/won't provide for the pilot.

Naomi
Security Architect
Redwood Inference
